question: Can boosting be parallelized, i.e. run in few rounds of weak-learner calls, without an exponential increase in total work?
contributions: Theorem 1: lower bound on the parallel complexity (p rounds, t queries per round) of any weak-to-strong learner.
Theorem 2: a single-round weak-to-strong learner using exp(O(d gamma^-2 ln m)) parallel weak-learner queries whose generalization matches AdaBoost, showing the lower bound is near tight.

results.claim: AdaBoost needs Theta(gamma^-2 ln m) sequential iterations, so its parallel complexity is (Theta(gamma^-2 ln m), 1).
results.source: known AdaBoost analysis, cited via Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David 2014
results.setup: gamma-weak learner, VC-dimension d hypothesis set, m training samples
results.quote: It thus has parallel complexity (Θ(γ−2 ln m), 1).

results.claim: Main lower bound: any weak-to-strong learner either uses exp(Omega(d)) rounds, or at least min{exp(Omega(d/gamma^2)), exp(exp(Omega(d)))} queries per round, or has expected error at least exp(-O(p max{gamma, ln(tp) gamma^2/d})).
results.setup: Theorem 1, worst-case domain, concept and gamma-weak learner with hypothesis set of VC-dimension d; learner A has parallel complexity (p,t); queries may be arbitrary distributions computable from data and earlier hypotheses
results.note: Theorem 1 itself is typeset with ligature/math characters; the proof setup restates the bound as nu.

results.claim: With constant rounds, matching AdaBoost's error needs t = exp(Omega(d gamma^-2 ln m)) queries per round.
results.setup: p = O(1) rounds, error target comparable to AdaBoost bound (1)

results.claim: To reach AdaBoost-comparable error with error exp(-O(p gamma)), rounds must be Omega(gamma^-1 ln m), only a factor gamma fewer than AdaBoost.
results.setup: Theorem 1 with polynomially many queries per round
results.quote: requires p = Ω(γ−1 ln m). This is only a γ factor less than AdaBoost.

results.claim: A single-round algorithm exists with parallel complexity (1, exp(O(d gamma^-2 ln m))) and AdaBoost-matching generalization error.
results.setup: Theorem 2; any concept, gamma-weak learner with VC-dimension d hypothesis set, any distribution, m samples
results.quote: A has parallel complexity (1, exp(O(dγ−2 ln m)))

results.claim: Sampled Boosting queries the weak learner on every uniform distribution over multisets of size a*d*gamma^-2 drawn from the training set, giving at most m^(a d gamma^-2) queries.
results.setup: Algorithm 1, a is a large enough constant
results.quote: there are no more than madγ−2 = exp(O(dγ−2 ln m)) such queries

results.claim: Sampled Boosting runs K = 16 gamma^-2 ln m rounds and yields a voting classifier with every training margin at least gamma/16.
results.setup: Algorithm 1 with K = 16 gamma^-2 ln m, w = 1/2 ln((1/2+gamma/4)/(1/2-gamma/4)), sample size n = a d gamma^-2; Lemmas 4 and 5
results.quote: We invoke Algorithm 1 with the training data set S as well as a number of rounds K = 16γ−2 ln m.
results.note: Margin gamma/16 is stated in the Sec 3 intro and Lemma 4.

results.claim: Long and Servedio's earlier bound p = Omega(gamma^-2 ln m) holds only for filtering-based query distributions and a weak-learner hypothesis set whose VC-dimension grows with m; the new single-round algorithm circumvents it.
results.quote: regardless of the number of calls per round t

limits: Purely theoretical: no experiments, no code, no runtime measurements.
Lower bound is worst case over a constructed domain, concept and weak learner; it says nothing about specific data or practical boosters.
Gap remains between rounds lower bound gamma^-1 ln m and AdaBoost's gamma^-2 ln m; authors leave partial parallelization open.
The single-round algorithm still does sequential work in O(gamma^-2 ln m) post-processing rounds (inference only), and its query count is exponential, so it is not practical.
The weak-learner query model abstracts training; it does not cover parallelism inside one weak learner (for example parallel tree construction in XGBoost/LightGBM).

terms.definition: given a constant number of samples m0 from any unknown distribution D, with constant probability returns h with L_D(h) <= 1/2 - gamma
for any 0 < eps, delta < 1 there is m(eps, delta) such that with probability at least 1 - delta it returns h with L_D(h) <= eps
a weak-to-strong learner invokes its weak learner in only p rounds, querying up to t distributions per round; queries may depend only on S, c(S) and hypotheses from earlier rounds
a sample T such that for all h in H the empirical error on T is within epsilon of the error under D

code.snippet: D_1 uniform; w = 1/2 ln((1/2+gamma/4)/(1/2-gamma/4)); n = a d gamma^-2; for k=1..K: draw T_k ~ D_k^n; h_k = h_{T_k}; while L_{D_k}(h_k) > 1/2 - gamma/4 redraw; D_{k+1}(i) = D_k(i) exp(-w c(x_i) h_k(x_i)) / Z_k; return g(x) = (1/K) sum_i h_i(x)
